text:
jordan: heads-up — we're seeing pods stuck Pending in eu-west-1 that require GPUs but cluster-autoscaler isn't launching nodes for gpu-pool-prod. Nothing obvious in CA logs. Anyone else seeing this?

mica: saw same earlier. kubectl describe shows scheduling fail: "0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match taint, 2 Insufficient accelerators."

sam: could be two-fold: taint mismatch between nodepool and pod tolerations, and the new zone hit GPU quota limits. Can you paste the pod and nodepool snippets?

jordan: pod tolerations look correct. snippet from kubectl describe (condensed):
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age    From               Message
  ----     ------             ----   ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   3m     default-scheduler  0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match taint, 2 Insufficient accelerators.
```

mica: sharing the terraform node_pool config we currently use for gpu-pool-prod (approx):
```hcl
resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu_pool" {
  node_config {
    machine_type = "n1-standard-16"
    accelerators { type = "nvidia-tesla-a100" count = 1 }
    taint { key = "dedicated" value = "gpu" effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }
    labels = { gpu = "true" }
  }
  autoscaling { min_node_count = 1 max_node_count = 4 }
}
```

olivia: two quick checks: 1) cloud quota for GPU GPUs in eu-west can silently block provisioning — check quota API/console; 2) CA autodiscovery for node groups must match the terraform node pool naming or CA won't scale it. Are we using node group tags?

sam: on the CA/helm side, our values currently are close to defaults. I think we should enable balancing across similar node groups and set expander to least-waste to prefer adding nodes that actually satisfy GPUs. Suggested values.yaml snippet:
```yaml
extraArgs:
  balance-similar-node-groups: ""
  expander: least-waste
  scale-down-unneeded-time: 10m
  skip-nodes-with-local-storage: false
nodeSelector: {}
rbac:
  create: true
```

mica: also propose increasing max_node_count to 10 for burst periods and adding a tiny buffer pool in eu-west (1 reserved GPU node) so transient scheduling spikes don't stall. We can run it as a small, always-on tainted pool with lower-cost preemptible instances as fallback.

olivia: caution: preemptible/spot GPUs can get reclaimed quickly in eu-west; good as fallback but need a 1-node warm pool to avoid cold-start for latency-sensitive workloads. Also check subnet IP quotas — provisioning errors there have looked like provisioning failures recently.

infra-bot: ci/cd: helm-chart "cluster-autoscaler" build passed for branch fix/ca-euw-balance — https://ci.internal/repo/7654 (deployed to staging) :rocket:

jordan: action items: 1) mica will open terraform PR to bump max_node_count, add a gpu-buffer-eu nodepool (tainted + preemptible fallback), and ensure node_pool names include the CA autodiscovery tag. 2) sam will PR a helm values tweak (balance-similar-node-groups + expander). 3) olivia will check GPU quota + subnet IP quotas and post back.

mica: will do PR today, assign reviewers.

sam: I'll run a staging canary once infra-bot finishes the chart rollout. :thumbsup:

olivia: checking quotas now, will DM results.

jordan: thanks team — tagging @here to keep awareness.
